newsitem.title: UK: LME zinc ends PM kerb stronger, copper softer.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc ends PM kerb stronger, copper softer.

text.p: Whippy base metals rebounded from lows on Tuesday afternoon, although copper and aluminium failed to recover gains from an early strong surge.
Nickel, however, was the weakest of the lot, ending down $210 near its lows in a market deflated by news downplaying the risk of a prolonged strike at Russia's Norilsk Nickel.
In contrast zinc, which zipped to fresh 4-1/2 year highs on speculative buying and producer short covering in early trading, held onto most of its rally gains and posted a strong close.
The market had mostly absorbed good forward selling throughout the day, although traders anticipated continued scale-up selling in the near future.
Three months zinc ended the London Metal Exchange (LME) afternoon kerb at $1,250 per tonne, up $11 from Monday.
Copper, however, slipped below the $2,400 level on overhead selling after hitting an early fresh nine-month peak and was unable to clamber above it again.
"People were disappointed with the small stocks drawdown (1,175 tonnes). Copper was erratic -- it wasn't a good close," a trader said.
It finished the kerb at $2,395, a decline of $13 from Monday but up about $10 from the day's low.
Near term support was expected to emerge at $2,385 area, while resistance was at the day's high of $2,420, traders said.
Wednesday's options declaration was expected to pass quietly as open interest was insignificant, they added.
Aluminium prices followed a similar pattern, initially racing to 14-month high of $1,701, then turning back on profit taking.
It ended little changed at $1,686, down $4.
Nickel was last at $8,100, compared to Monday's $2,310.
Lead and tin were mostly quiet, but they also felt the crunch hitting the other base metals and ended the day in the minus column.
Lead edged below the $700 level in kerb trading and ended at $697, a $5 decline. Cash/threes remained in backwardation due to tightness in April dates and was last at $13/$16.
Tin was down $10 at $5,850, while alloy was last at $1,555, off $5. --Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
